title: 2. Localize frozen JOINT's reset weakness without another rollout
hypothesis: Expanded resets expose a transverse-position capture-basin boundary, so initial displacement perpendicular to the pen axis predicts frozen JOINT failure beyond axial displacement and tilt.

prediction.against: R-129: frozen JOINT on the lowest transverse-displacement quartile of expanded resets
prediction.rationale: Compare highest versus lowest transverse-displacement quartiles, standardized over predeclared axial-displacement and tilt tertiles on common support. A 0.15 success deficit would localize a substantial part of D-089's 0.281 reset penalty. D-092 tested training-distribution coverage, not this geometric localization; this is descriptive robustness analysis, not authorization for capture-controller development.

protocol.command: gpu run 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && timeout 900s python -u scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --study reset_geometry_audit'
code_changes: lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/reset_geometry_audit.py (new, archive only; registered in scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py with a block in config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml). Primary archive: R-129's 512 frozen-JOINT cases under reset scale 1.5 (logs/pen_spin/r129_frozen_robustness/cells/s<seed>/joint@reset_1.5_cell.json, 4 manifests). Separate replication, never pooled and never chosen between after results: R-133's 1,536 frozen-JOINT cases under reset scale 1.5 (logs/pen_spin/r133_reset_mixture/confirmation/expanded/s<seed>/joint_cell.json, 12 manifests).

Initial states are reconstructed, not recorded: a case's reset is cases.resolve_placements(manifest) times the recorded reset scale (position offset = rows 0-2 times the env's position noise; tilt = the rotation built from rows 3-4 as the runner writes it). Frozen definitions: the initial pen long axis is the tilted x axis; axial displacement = |offset . axis|; transverse displacement = norm of the offset perpendicular to the axis; tilt = the initial rotation angle. Within each archive: transverse quartiles, axial tertiles and tilt tertiles by rank (ties by case order).

Registered quantity (success_rate): sustained success in the highest transverse quartile minus the lowest, standardized over the axial-by-tilt strata present in both extreme quartiles with weights proportional to the pooled count of the two quartiles in each stratum; a case-level 95% interval from the per-stratum binomial variances. Report support counts and the coverage of the common support (at least 6 of 9 strata and 60% of both quartiles' cases, otherwise inconclusive). Supported (a decrease of at least 0.15) with the upper bound <= -0.15; refuted with the lower bound > -0.15; otherwise inconclusive. Also report unstandardized success by quartile for transverse, axial and tilt.
Ceiling: 0 simulator episodes, 0 LLM calls, 15 minutes; no new seeds, manifests, fitting or replacement rollouts; reconstruction failures are reported, not patched.

falsified_by: The lower 95% interval bound on high-minus-low standardized success is above -0.15. Failure of common support or unavailable initial-state records makes the audit inconclusive rather than permitting replacement rollouts.

approval.note: I accept the corrected study entry point, reconstructed initial geometry and separately reported R-133 replication; this localizes frozen JOINT's reset weakness descriptively rather than repeating D-092's training intervention. controls.reconstruction: placement vector x reset scale, as runner._write_placements writes it; not a recorded state
controls.units: displacements in units of the env's reset position noise; tilt in radians

result.notes: Archive only; no episode, no model call; definitions committed (867bf43) before the audit ran; initial geometry is reconstructed from the manifest placement vectors times the 1.5 reset scale, not recorded. REGISTERED (primary archive, R-129's 512 frozen-JOINT cases at 1.5x): success in the highest transverse-displacement quartile minus the lowest, standardized over all nine axial x tilt strata (full common support): -0.056, 95% interval [-0.177, +0.064]. It spans both zero and -0.15: INCONCLUSIVE. The predeclared separate replication (R-133's 1,536 frozen-JOINT cases at 1.5x): -0.172 [-0.239, -0.105], a clear deficit whose interval still spans -0.15, so the registered magnitude is not established there either; the two archives are not pooled. NOT REGISTERED, descriptive, identical in both archives: the failures track the pen's initial TILT far more than its displacement. Success by tilt quartile (lowest to highest): 0.812 / 0.594 / 0.383 / 0.156 in R-129 and 0.815 / 0.526 / 0.326 / 0.182 in R-133; by transverse quartile 0.516 / 0.531 / 0.453 / 0.445 and 0.523 / 0.503 / 0.456 / 0.367; by axial quartile it is flat (0.43-0.56 and 0.43-0.52). So at 1.5x resets the frozen JOINT keeps its nominal success (about 0.8) on the least-tilted quarter of cases and fails five times in six on the most-tilted quarter; the wide-reset weakness of D-089 is mostly an initial-orientation effect. This was not the registered hypothesis and is an association over reconstructed geometry; it needs its own prospective test before it is relied on.

verdicts.reasoning: By the frozen rule the primary archive gives -0.056 [-0.177, +0.064] for the standardized highest-minus-lowest transverse-quartile success: it spans both zero and the registered -0.15. The separate 1,536-case replication gives -0.172 [-0.239, -0.105], a real deficit that still spans -0.15, and the archives are not pooled. The transverse-boundary hypothesis is therefore not established at its registered size. The unregistered, descriptive pattern is much larger and replicates exactly: success falls with initial tilt from about 0.81 to about 0.17 across quartiles in both archives, while axial displacement is flat.
verdicts.next_experiment: The wide-reset weakness looks like an initial-orientation effect; that is a new mechanism to test prospectively (for example frozen JOINT on resets that scale tilt and position separately) and, if it holds, a capture-authority question beyond this direction's scope. Hand the choice of direction back to the user.

verdicts.reasoning: The named lowest-quartile control was measured, and both archives retained all nine strata with full common-support coverage [logs/pen_spin/r135_reset_geometry/summary.json]. The primary standardized high-minus-low success_rate was -0.0564, with a 95% interval of [-0.1768, +0.0639]; it includes zero, so it provides no evidence of a directional difference [logs/pen_spin/r135_reset_geometry/summary.json]. That interval also crosses -0.15, satisfying neither the registered support rule nor the falsification rule [logs/pen_spin/r135_reset_geometry/summary.json]. The separately reported replication shows a deficit of -0.1718 [-0.2385, -0.1050], but its interval also crosses -0.15, leaving the predicted magnitude unresolved without pooling or substituting archives [logs/pen_spin/r135_reset_geometry/summary.json]. The descriptive tilt gradient does not establish that initial orientation causes most of the expanded-reset weakness [logs/pen_spin/r135_reset_geometry/summary.json].

Initial states are not recorded in cells but are exactly reconstructable: a case's reset is its manifest placement vector times the reset scale (cases.resolve_placements; position offset rows 0-2, tilt rows 3-4), and R-133's smoke verified the written offsets to 1.5e-6. (2) Data: R-129 has only 512 JOINT cases at 1.5x (4 manifests), too few for 4 quartiles x 9 strata. D-092's archive adds 1,536 fresh frozen-JOINT cases at 1.5x (12 manifests). Register R-129's 512 as the named source and R-133's 1,536 as a predeclared replication reported beside it, with the same frozen definitions: transverse displacement = the component of the initial position offset perpendicular to the pen's initial long axis, axial = the component along it, tilt = the initial rotation magnitude; quartiles and tertiles computed within each archive; standardization over the axial x tilt strata present in both extreme quartiles.

advisor.reasoning: I accept both implementer corrections: the MetaWorld summarizer is unsuitable, and R-133 supplies a useful separately reported archive replication without new rollouts. Reconstructing initial geometry from manifest placements is appropriate, but sparse common support remains the weakest point, especially for R-129's four manifests. This can describe reset vulnerability after R-134, not establish a causal capture boundary or authorize controller development.
